transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I blew up at one of the younger volunteers over a crooked tablecloth. I don't usually speak to people that way, and it bothered me.
Would you say this kind of quick temper or irritability has been part of how you've generally been for years, or is this a new change that's only been happening recently?
No, that isn't how I usually am. The other day, with the tablecloth—I just snapped at that young volunteer. I don't normally talk to people that way.
Over what period of time have you been noticing this irritability or feeling different from your usual self—has it been days, weeks, or longer?
About a week now—ever since that robbery outside the bank.
Since the robbery, have you been having any unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about that event?
Yes. Out of nowhere, I hear that man's rough voice in my head, or I see the donation envelope hitting the ground—even when I'm just sitting at my kitchen table.
Since the robbery, have you found yourself avoiding places, people, or situations that remind you of what happened?
Yes. I've been taking the long way around so I don't have to pass the bank. And I haven't gone into the festival storage room either—it just brings the whole thing too close.
Since the robbery, have you noticed times when you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, like you were in a daze or watching things happen from outside your body?
No, I haven’t really felt detached like that. I’ve felt shaken up, but I know where I am and what’s going on around me.
Did these feelings of being shaken up, the flashbacks, and the avoidance start right away—within a day of the robbery—or did they come on gradually after some time had passed?
It started right away, after the robbery. It’s been about a week now.
Since the robbery, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually jumpy or easily startled, having trouble falling or staying asleep, or feeling constantly on guard even in safe situations?
Yes. A car backfired near the senior center, and I jumped so hard my chest hurt. My hands were shaking for a few minutes afterward.
Have you been having any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep since the robbery?
Yes. I get into bed tired, but then I lie there listening for every little noise. And I wake up before dawn feeling like I barely slept at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient developed a cluster of distressing symptoms within days following a clearly identifiable traumatic event (armed robbery witnessed outside the bank), including intrusive memories/flashbacks, avoidance of reminders, hyperarousal (exaggerated startle response, hypervigilance, insomnia), and irritability/anger outbursts. Symptoms began immediately after the trauma and have persisted for about one week, which is consistent with Acute Stress Reaction (F43.0) rather than PTSD (which requires symptom duration beyond one month) or Adjustment Disorder (which does not require a life-threatening/traumatic stressor with this symptom profile). No dissociative depersonalization/derealization was endorsed, but the overall symptom pattern and temporal course support F43.0.
